properties.areaDesc: Alexander, NC; Catawba, NC; Iredell, NC
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 12 at 8:58PM EDT until October 13 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...Portions of Alexander, Catawba, and Iredell Counties, along
the shores of Lookout Shoals Lake.

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas including
residential yards, docks, and boat-launch areas is ongoing along
the shores of Lookout Shoals Lake. Residents should take immediate
actions to protect property adjacent to the lake and monitor
messaging from county Emergency Management agencies.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 857 PM EDT, Levels of the lakes of the Catawba River remain
elevated as water continues to move downriver following the heavy
rain event over the weekend. While Lookout Shoals Lake has
receded since Sunday afternoon, it remains at Action stage and
some flooding of low-lying areas near the lake shore could
continue through at least Tuesday morning.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. Please obey all barricades and heed any evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Myakka River At Myakka River State Park affecting Sarasota County.

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Citrus, Levy and Marion
Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.2 feet
tomorrow evening. It will then fall below flood stage early
Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

through flooded areas.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 12 at 1:50PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by Thursday night. Widespread showers may
be heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of thunderstorms.
Landslides will also be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
Impacts could begin as early as Thursday and are expected to
persist through the weekend. While there is still uncertainty in
the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan now for wet
conditions that could persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Thursday night through Sunday

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 2:53PM PDT until October 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco and
Monterey Bays.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
